artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ be finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}$ satisfying
$$\min\{|A_1|, |A_2|, \ldots, |A_n|\} \geq n+1.$$
Is it always possible to choose elements $a_1 \in A_1, a_2 \in A_2, \ldots, a_n \in A_n$ such that, for every non-empty subset $I \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$,
$$\sum_{i \in I} a_i \neq 0?$$
(The bound $n+1$, if correct, would be best possible: there exist many collections $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ with $|A_1| = \cdots = |A_n| = n$ for which no such choice exists.)
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, attributed to N. Alon, asks whether the sharp lower bound $n+1$ on $\min|A_i|$ suffices. The best known result, due to Alon and Ruzsa ("Non-averaging Subsets and Non-vanishing Transversals", J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 1999), only establishes the conclusion under the stronger hypothesis $\min|A_i| \geq C_\varepsilon n^{1+\varepsilon}$. No subsequent resolution of the original $n+1$ version appears in the literature, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Non-averaging Subsets and Non-vanishing Transversals - Princeton University
status_evidence.snippet: If A_1,...,A_m are m subsets of cardinality at least m^{1+ε} each, then there exist a_i ∈ A_i so that every nonempty subset sum is nonzero.
status_evidence.claim: The best known bound is m^{1+ε}, not the conjectured m+1, indicating the original conjecture remains open.
